skill.name: new-leader-alerts
skill.description: Compare VP and C-level rosters at target companies against a saved snapshot. Use Leadsets to check candidate roles and include work emails with their reported status when available.
skill.summary: Track newly observed executives and promotions at target companies.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The documented Leadsets search sends target company domains to an external service. The other static hits are Markdown, optional links, or prose, with no evidence of shell execution, environment access, reconnaissance, or prompt injection. The workflow lacks a recipient check and a clear rule for partial snapshots, and its verification instructions conflict.

remediation.issue: Alerts can expose work emails and account targeting to unintended readers.
remediation.suggestion: Preview the destination and fields before posting to a shared system. Require approval for that audience and omit work emails by default from shared alerts.

remediation.issue: The workflow gives inconsistent instructions for missing role checks and email verification.
remediation.suggestion: Require matching current-role evidence before labeling an alert confirmed. Report missing enrichment separately and label an email verified only when its returned status is verified.

remediation.issue: An incomplete run could replace the last complete snapshot.
remediation.suggestion: Save partial progress separately. Replace the active snapshot only after all target accounts are checked, and flag incomplete runs in the output.

semantic_findings.title: Shared Alerts Lack Recipient Checks
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can publish work emails and leadership changes to shared tools through the agent connection. It does not require checking who can read them.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Role and Email Verification Rules
semantic_findings.description: The workflow keeps alerts when enrichment returns no match, yet requires current-role evidence for every alert. It also describes enriched emails as verified despite requiring explicit status checks elsewhere.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly permits an alert without enrichment evidence and elsewhere requires that evidence. It makes conflicting claims about the verification status of enriched emails.

semantic_findings.title: Partial Run Can Compromise the Comparison Baseline
semantic_findings.description: The workflow saves progress on a rate limit but does not specify when that progress may replace the complete snapshot. Missing accounts could appear as departures or generate duplicate alerts later.

content.user_title: Track New Leaders at Target Accounts
content.value_statement: Checking target accounts manually for executive changes takes time. This skill compares Leadsets results with a saved roster and shows which leaders are newly observed or appear to have been promoted.
actual_capabilities: Check the remaining Leadsets search and enrichment allowance before a run.
Search company domains for VP and C-level leaders, with optional title or function filters.
Create a baseline on the first run and compare later results to identify new names and apparent promotions.
Check candidate roles with Leadsets and report available work emails alongside their returned status.
Save a leader snapshot and deliver alerts as a CSV or through a connected tool.
limitations: The skill sees changes only after they appear in Leadsets and does not verify official start dates.
Search and enrichment use account allowances. A rate limit can leave a run incomplete.
Work email and current-role evidence are not available for every candidate.
Recurring runs need a separate scheduler. The skill does not send outreach.

use_cases.title: Review Leadership at Named Accounts
use_cases.description: Compare the latest results with your last snapshot before account planning. Review newly observed leaders and check which accounts had no results.

use_cases.title: Watch for Product and Engineering Leaders
use_cases.description: Track product and engineering leaders at a short list of companies. Review new entries without including work emails in the report.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Recurring Account Snapshot
use_cases.description: Use an existing scheduler to refresh the executive roster. Track coverage and record usage before replacing the previous complete snapshot.

prompt_templates.title: Create Your First Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the company domains in my CSV to create a VP and C-level baseline. Save the snapshot and summarize coverage without sending alerts.
prompt_templates.scenario: First run with no previous snapshot.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Against a Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this domain list with my last leader snapshot. Separate newly observed leaders from apparent promotions and list accounts that returned no results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Manual follow-up using the same account list.

prompt_templates.title: Narrow the Search and Review Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my remaining Leadsets allowance and test the revenue leadership filters on one account. Estimate the cost before searching the full list.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a focused comparison within the service allowance.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Scheduled Check With Approval
prompt_templates.prompt: For this scheduled run, compare the account list with the last complete snapshot. Show a preview without emails and wait for approval before posting. Keep partial results separate from the baseline.
prompt_templates.scenario: An existing scheduler and a destination with known access permissions.

output_examples.input: Create a VP and C-level baseline for my 12 target domains.
output_examples.output: Baseline created. Checked 12 accounts and found 46 leaders. One account returned no leaders. No new-leader alerts were sent.

output_examples.input: Compare this week's results with the previous snapshot.
output: Checked 12 accounts. Two newly observed leaders and one apparent promotion matched current-role data.
Leadsets marked one work email verified and one catch-all. No email was available for the third leader.
One leader was not found in the latest search. The report lists this as a possible departure, not a confirmed one.

best_practices: Test the role filters on one company domain and check the remaining allowance before a full run.
Keep the last complete snapshot until all intended accounts have been checked.
Review the destination permissions and share only the contact fields the recipients need.
anti_patterns: Treating a first run as evidence of new hires.
Calling a catch-all or unknown email verified, or treating the discovery date as an official start date.
Posting work emails to a broad channel without checking who can see them.

faq.question: What do I need to run this skill?
faq.answer: Provide company domains and a Leadsets account. Connect the Leadsets MCP server to your agent or use a Leadsets API key for REST access.

faq.question: Does the first run send alerts?
faq.answer: No. The first run saves the current leaders as a baseline for later comparisons.

faq.question: Can I choose which roles to track?
faq.answer: Yes. The default covers VP and C-level roles across all functions. You can narrow the search by function or title.

faq.question: Does an alert mean the person just started?
faq.answer: No. The first-seen date is when the skill detected the change, not the person's official start date.

faq.question: Are all work emails verified?
faq.answer: No. An email is verified only when Leadsets explicitly returns that status. Catch-all and unknown are separate statuses, and some records have no email.

faq.question: Can this send weekly Slack alerts?
faq.answer: Use a separate scheduler for weekly runs and a connected Slack account for delivery. Confirm the destination and audience before posting.
